title: International Day of Older Persons 2026: the Age of Longevity theme
dek: October 1 is the UN's International Day of Older Persons. The 2026 theme asks how health, work and housing can adapt to longer lives.
keyPoints: October 1 is the UN International Day of Older Persons.

WHO webinar on the UN International Day of Older Persons 2026: The Age of Longevity
Longer Lives Creating Risks, Opportunities, Transforming Economies, Societies, Secretary-General Says

body: Today, October 1, is the United Nations International Day of Older Persons. Early risers are often older adults, so this is a fitting hour to mark it.

The 2026 theme is "The Age of Longevity: Rethinking Systems for Longer Lives." The UN calls the aging of the world's population one of the most significant demographic changes of our time. Its message is that longer lives bring real opportunities, and also require rethinking how health systems, job markets, social protection, education and housing support people across their whole lives.

The World Health Organization is holding a webinar on the theme today. The UN's main event takes place on October 8 at UN Headquarters in New York, where panels will look at healthy aging and prevention, employment that includes older workers, pensions and social protection, and care that connects health and social services.

For individuals, the theme is a reminder that aging well is a shared project. It involves the older people in our lives, and it also involves our own future selves. Practical steps can be small: helping a parent set up online access to their Medicare or Social Security account, asking an older neighbor if they need anything during this week's heat in Southern California, or looking into volunteer programs that pair generations.
Today, reach out to one older person you know and ask them a question about their life that you have never asked before. It is a simple way to honor the day and learn something too.
